subject: series
synopsis: Trade paperback collections reprinting classic Doug Moench and Bill Sienkiewicz Moon Knight stories from the 1980s, capturing the definitive Bronze Age version of the character at his most compelling and psychologically complex.
author: Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: Takuma Morishige's manga follows Rumi Yokoi, perpetually distracted from class by her seat-neighbor Seki's increasingly elaborate, absurd solo projects — robotics, shogi, family drama played out with erasers. A perfect single-joke premise executed with endless imagination.
author: Takuma Morishige

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's company-wide crossover involving the sinister Mys-Tech corporation, combining their British characters (Dark Guard, Death's Head, Motormouth) in a crossover that tested the limits of the interconnected Marvel UK universe.
author: Dan Abnett

subject: series
synopsis: A Mystic Arcana one-shot focusing on Nico Minoru, the Staff of One-wielding Runaway, exploring the mystical heritage of Marvel's teenage sorcerers through ancient artifacts and dark magical history.

subject: series
synopsis: A Behemoth Comics series with fantasy and mystical elements.

subject: series
synopsis: Tasuku Karasuma's cyberpunk noir manga follows Juzo Inui, a Resolver (fixer) with a giant revolver for a head, navigating post-war society where human 'Extended' with machine augmentations are social outcasts. A stylish neo-noir with hard-boiled atmosphere.
author: Tasuku Karasuma

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis and Juan José Ryp's Avatar Press series asking what it would take to give ordinary people superpowers, with grim answers involving extreme body modification and psychological destruction. Characteristically Ellis in its unflinching examination of superhero violence.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: Jay Faerber's 2002 Noble Causes mini: Liz Donnelly, widowed soon after marrying hero Race Noble, struggles to find her place in his superpowered family.

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Beatty's Wildstorm series connecting the various Wildstorm universes through a government simulation program, serving as a prelude to the Wildstorm line-wide revamp. An interesting concept delivered with moderate execution.
author: Scott Beatty

subject: series
synopsis: Dan DiDio and Keith Giffen's 2011 New 52 O.M.A.C.: Kevin Kho becomes Brother Eye's One-Machine Attack Construct in a Kirby-styled romp.

subject: series
synopsis: Bruce Jones and Renato Guedes's 2006 OMAC: Michael Costner, transformed into a cybernetic OMAC, flees Brother Eye after Infinite Crisis.
author: Bruce Jones

subject: series
synopsis: Garon Tsuchiya and Nobuaki Minegishi's psychological thriller about a man released after 10 inexplicable years of imprisonment who obsessively seeks to learn why he was held captive and by whom. Relentlessly plotted and deeply unsettling; the basis for Park Chan-wook's celebrated 2003 film.
author: Garon Tsuchiya

subject: series
synopsis: Sylvain Runberg and Serge Pellé's Cinebook space opera following a human-alien diplomatic agent duo on interplanetary missions; well-drawn and competently plotted if not groundbreaking, a solid entry in the Franco-Belgian sci-fi tradition.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang's time-travel adventure following four paper delivery girls in 1988 who get caught up in a war between time-traveling factions, hopping across different eras of American history.
author: Brian K. Vaughan

subject: series
synopsis: Hitoshi Iwaaki's landmark manga about high school student Shinichi Izumi, whose hand is taken over by an alien parasite named Migi. Their reluctant symbiosis forces Shinichi to confront increasingly disturbing questions about humanity's place in nature as other parasites seek to consume human hosts wholesale.
author: Hitoshi Iwaaki

subject: series
synopsis: A deluxe full-color reprint edition of Hitoshi Iwaaki's landmark manga Parasyte, presenting the classic body-horror story about alien parasites and human identity in newly colorized volumes.
author: Hitoshi Iwaaki

subject: series
synopsis: Philip Gelatt and Brett Weldele's Dark Horse series about a group of superintelligent teenagers framed for destroying the world's satellite network, navigating betrayal and survival in space. A smart SF premise with interesting character work.
author: Philip Gelatt

subject: series
synopsis: Nate Cosby and Ben McCool's Image Comics espionage thriller about a group of Cuban sleeper agents trained in the 1960s who are reactivated in modern America to fulfill a long-delayed mission. Cold War paranoia updated for contemporary politics.
author: Nate Cosby

subject: series
synopsis: Naoki Urasawa's masterful reimagining of Osamu Tezuka's 'The Greatest Robot on Earth' arc from Astro Boy, retold as a noir mystery following robot detective Gesicht who investigates the murders of the world's most powerful robots. Urasawa elevates the source material into a profound meditation on humanity, war, and what it means to feel.
author: Naoki Urasawa

subject: series
synopsis: Walt Kelly's complete Pogo newspaper strip — a masterwork of satirical political cartooning and naturalist warmth, following the inhabitants of Okefenokee Swamp in strips that skewered 1950s McCarthy-era America.
author: Walt Kelly

subject: series
synopsis: Paper Films sci-fi action with indie sensibility and experimental panel layouts.

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Rucka's spy thriller series with political intrigue and action.
author: Greg Rucka

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Starlin's DC cosmic series pitting the space empires of Rann and Thanagar against each other while a new religious war threatens the universe. Part of the ambitious DC cosmic line Starlin led in the late 2000s.
author: Jim Starlin

subject: series
synopsis: Continuation of Raven Xingtao's all-female pirate crew adventures in the Princeless universe, maintaining Jeremy Whitley's trademark blend of feminist themes, swashbuckling action, and sharp humor. The series grew a devoted following for its diverse cast and genuine heart.
author: Jeremy Whitley

subject: series
synopsis: An Alterna Comics series with retro sci-fi and adventure themes.

subject: series
synopsis: Okushou and Shizumu Watanabe's survival manga about players trapped inside a social media platform where losing followers means dying in real life. A fast-paced death-game manga that uses social media mechanics as horror.
author: Okushou

subject: series
synopsis: A crossover series that comedically and cleverly unites Red Sonja, Vampirella, and the Archie Comics characters Betty and Veronica.
author: Amy Chu

subject: series
synopsis: Keith Giffen's DC miniseries following the political struggles of Hell's various ruling factions — Neron, Blaze, Satanus, and others — in a conflict that spills over into the DC superhero world. Ambitious worldbuilding in a chaotic, dense story.
author: Keith Giffen

subject: series
synopsis: Darwyn Cooke's stunning adaptation of Richard Stark's heist novel in which Parker and a crew of specialists plan to rob an entire small town in a single night — a masterwork of design and noir storytelling.
author: Darwyn Cooke

subject: series
synopsis: A BOOM Studios adaptation of Frank Miller's unproduced RoboCop 3 screenplay, finally seeing publication in comics form after years in limbo. Of considerable interest as an artifact of what Miller had planned for the franchise, more violent and political than the produced film.
author: Frank Miller

subject: series
synopsis: A GFT universe series following Robyn Hood, a modern female reimagining of the Robin Hood legend who operates as a vigilante hero. One of Zenescope's more prominent spinoff characters with multiple miniseries and an ongoing.

subject: series
synopsis: Boom Studios/KaBOOM's licensed series continuing the adventures of the beloved Nickelodeon babies Tommy, Chuckie, Phil, Lil, and Angelica in new all-ages adventures. Captures the visual style and character dynamics of the animated series faithfully.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Minna Sundberg's Nordic post-apocalyptic webcomic: ninety years after a plague emptied the world, a small crew ventures into the silent, haunted lands beyond Iceland.

subject: series
synopsis: A four-issue miniseries casting Sabretooth in a bloody European thriller, as the feral mutant becomes entangled with a secret organization creating horrific biological experiments in the tradition of Frankenstein.
author: Daniel Way

subject: series
synopsis: A deluxe large-format reprint of Naoki Takeuchi's landmark magical girl manga, presenting the original Sailor Moon story in its definitive format. The manga that defined the magical girl genre and remains its most influential entry.
author: Naoko Takeuchi

subject: series
synopsis: A Heavy Metal series blending dark carnival atmosphere with action and surreal storytelling.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's black-and-white magazine featuring Conan the Barbarian, Man-Thing, and other pulp heroes in stories too mature for the Comics Code, representing Marvel's early foray into the magazine format.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first vertical Infinity Comic featuring Wolverine in brutal, action-focused stories that lean into the character's savage berserker nature, formatted for mobile reading.

subject: series
synopsis: John Smith's Vertigo series featuring Louis Sendak, a former 1940s superhero reawakened in the modern day who was always more sorcerer than superhero. A distinctive Vertigo take on the Golden Age hero concept with Smith's characteristically strange plotting.
author: John Smith

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's four-issue series about Alix Harrower, reluctant superhero, whose husband's fetish for superhero enhancements accidentally transforms her into the bulletproof Bulleteer. A sharp satire of superhero wish-fulfillment and fandom from Morrison's Seven Soldiers project.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Jake Jordan becomes the new Guardian and uncovers a conspiracy threatening Manhattan.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Klarion flees Limbo Town and discovers a disturbing world above ground.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's four-issue series about Sir Ystin, a female knight from Camelot transported to modern-day Los Angeles. Part of the Seven Soldiers project, blending Arthurian legend with superhero mythology.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's four-issue Zatanna spotlight from the Seven Soldiers of Victory project, following Zatanna into a world of pop-culture magic and confronting the responsibility of power. Morrison at his most accessible and playful with the character.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: V.E. Schwab's graphic-novel prequels to her Shades of Magic novels, following the young Antari magician Kell across the parallel Londons.

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first Infinity Comic following Shang-Chi and his siblings as they navigate family obligations, martial arts mastery, and shadowy conspiracies in a format designed for mobile vertical reading.

subject: series
synopsis: Rich Tommaso's Image series follows Gabby, a teenager convinced a werewolf killed her family, as her hunt blurs into surreal, drug-tinged nightmare. A stylized, off-kilter horror with bold flat colors.
author: Rich Tommaso

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Trevor Hairsine's 2003 Ultimate Six: Norman Osborn's Sinister Six break out of S.H.I.E.L.D. and clash with Spider-Man and the Ultimates.

subject: series
synopsis: Bryan Q. Miller's digital-first continuation of the Smallville TV series, picking up where the show left off with Clark finally in the Superman costume. Remarkably faithful to the show's characters and tone while expanding the universe to include Green Arrow, Batman, and other heroes.
author: Bryan Q. Miller

subject: series
synopsis: George Perez's CrossGen series starring Solus, an ancient and enormously powerful cosmic entity awakened in the CrossGen universe. A grand-scale cosmic adventure leaning into Perez's strengths with large casts and intricate page design.
author: George Perez

subject: series
synopsis: The second volume of Tom DeFalco's Spider-Girl series, following May 'Mayday' Parker as the daughter of Peter Parker in the MC2 alternate future universe. DeFalco's commitment to classic superhero storytelling found a loyal audience despite consistently low sales.
author: Tom DeFalco

subject: series
synopsis: Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale's heartfelt love letter to Spider-Man's earliest years, following Peter Parker as he reminisces about Gwen Stacy and his complicated feelings for Mary Jane through rose-tinted nostalgia for Marvel's Silver Age.
author: Jeph Loeb

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries by Elliott Kalan where Spider-Man joins the Jean Grey School as a guidance counselor, pairing him with a class of troublemaking young mutants for a comic and action-driven school story.
author: Elliott Kalan

subject: series
synopsis: A Marvel limited series pairing two of the publisher's most popular characters in a story involving time travel and memory manipulation. Competent execution of an inherently crowd-pleasing premise.
author: Brett Matthews

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's 2010 Spike ongoing by Brian Lynch: the vampire Spike battles demons and old enemies in a continuation of Angel.

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first horror-inflected Infinity Comic series featuring Spider-Man facing supernatural and psychological threats, blending classic web-slinging action with genuine frights in vertical mobile format.

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's photo-comic series using digitally manipulated screenshots from the original Star Trek television series to tell new stories in the style of the classic Gold Key comics era. A loving and technically inventive tribute to TOS that manages to capture the period's storytelling tone while expanding on untold adventures of Kirk and crew.
author: John Byrne

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's reprint collection gathering classic Dark Horse Comics Star Wars Legends stories set during the Imperial era, making key Expanded Universe tales available to modern readers in affordable trade format.
author: Randy Stradley

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's reprint anthology collecting Dark Horse's Expanded Universe stories set in the New Republic era following Return of the Jedi, including tales of the Rebellion's transition to galactic governance.
author: Ryder Windham

subject: series
synopsis: A Marvel ongoing series following the galaxy's deadliest hired guns - Valance, Bossk, Boba Fett, and others - as they navigate shifting loyalties between the Empire, the Rebellion, and criminal syndicates during the Galactic Civil War era.
author: Ethan Sacks

subject: series
synopsis: A Heroic Age limited series following Steve Rogers in his new role as head of SHIELD's security operations after the Siege of Asgard, written by Ed Brubaker as a WWII-tinged espionage thriller with art by Dale Eaglesham.
author: Ed Brubaker

subject: series
synopsis: Strangelands is a Humanoids sci-fi series about two strangers who are inexplicably drawn together and must unravel the cosmic mystery binding their fates. Blending action and speculative fiction, it explores identity and connection in a world of strange phenomena.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's Strawberry Shortcake comics series reimagining the classic toy and cartoon character for a new generation.

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander's return to the Suicide Squad after years away, delivering the same morally complex mission-based storytelling and genuine threat of character death that defined his seminal 1987-1992 run. A powerful reminder of what the property can be at its best.
author: John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Millar and Leinil Francis Yu's story about a boy with multiple sclerosis who is granted the wish to become a Superman-style hero. More emotionally resonant than most Millarworld output; Yu's kinetic art suits the wish-fulfillment premise.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: Michael Kupperman's deeply absurdist anthology comic — dense, unpredictable, and wildly original humor that parodies pulp comics, old-time radio, and genre fiction with a surrealist intelligence unlike anything else in the medium.
author: Michael Kupperman

subject: series
synopsis: IDW anthology and spin-off series exploring side stories and character spotlights set in the main IDW TMNT universe. Expands the lore beyond the flagship series.

subject: series
synopsis: Rick Spears and Rob G's self-published 2001 series: two misfit teens strike back when their small town cracks down on comics.

subject: series
synopsis: Yui Yoshino's slice-of-life manga about a girl navigating friendships, summer, and early romantic feelings in a quiet, atmospheric way that captures the specific texture of adolescent summers.
author: Yui Yoshino

subject: series
synopsis: John Ridley and Georges Jeanty's prescient 1960s superhero political drama — the government-sponsored team of heroes cracks when a Black superhero joins the lineup and social forces tear the PR-manufactured team apart.
author: John Ridley

subject: series
synopsis: A spin-off manga from the main Ancient Magus' Bride series following different characters in the same magical world, expanding the mythology without the main couple.
author: Kore Yamazaki

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Casey's second Earth's Mightiest Heroes limited series revisiting the early days of the Avengers, filling in gaps in classic continuity with psychological depth and period-accurate detail. A companion to the equally strong first volume.
author: Joe Casey

subject: series
synopsis: Gabriel Benson and Mike Hawthorne's Image series reimagining the Sleeping Beauty fairy tale as a western adventure, with a gunslinger searching for the legendary sleeping beauty who is said to grant unimaginable power. A creative genre mashup.
author: Gabriel Benson

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Jurgens and Mike Perkins's DC Black Label series imagining Batman's very first year in 1939, with period-authentic crime noir aesthetics and a mystery involving Gotham's criminal underworld before the colorful supervillains arrived. A respectful, beautifully illustrated Elseworlds piece.
author: Dan Jurgens

subject: series
synopsis: Wendy and Richard Pini's epic fantasy saga collected in full, following the elf tribe the Wolfriders across thousands of years of struggle, love, and discovery in a prehistoric world.
author: Wendy Pini

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns and Ethan Van Sciver's 2009 The Flash: Rebirth: Barry Allen returns from the dead and confronts the Reverse-Flash, who rewrote his past.

subject: series
synopsis: Graphic novels based on the 2010 animated series: the Little Prince and the Fox travel to new planets to save the stars from the Snake.

subject: series
synopsis: Papercutz graphic novels of Nickelodeon's The Loud House: Lincoln Loud's chaotic life with ten sisters.

subject: series
synopsis: Jerry Frissen's continuation of Jodorowsky's Metabarons universe, following a new Metabaron in the far future with science fantasy grandeur and the operatic violence that defines the property. Respectfully extends the original vision for dedicated fans.
author: Jerry Frissen

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Abnett and I.N.J. Culbard's elegant Edwardian mystery: the British upper class became vampires to avoid zombification, and now a murder among the Young forces a detective to unravel class, death, and empire.
author: Dan Abnett

subject: series
synopsis: Ram V and Mike Perkins' 2021-2022 DC series following Jacob Kampling, a new host for the Swamp Thing entity, as he navigates the Parliament of Trees and the nature of green consciousness. A thoughtful new chapter in a venerable mythology.
author: Ram V

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries continuing the adventures of Ben Edlund's satirical superhero The Tick, parodying superhero genre conventions with absurdist humor and the Tick's relentlessly optimistic dimwittedness.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite Entertainment's adaptation of Robert Jordan's prequel novel depicting the young Moiraine and Lan before the events of the main Wheel of Time saga. Faithful to the source material with competent fantasy art.
author: Robert Jordan

subject: series
synopsis: Miniseries exploring Metropolis's history and supporting cast around Clark Kent.
author: John Byrne

subject: series
synopsis: Yves Sente's Thorgal Universe spinoff following the morally complex Kriss of Valnor — the beautiful and ruthless antagonist of the main Thorgal series — in her own adventures.
author: Yves Sente

subject: series
synopsis: Bob Wayne and Lewis Shiner's DC limited series featuring Rip Hunter and his companions on time-traveling adventures to save history. A serviceable time travel adventure that used the DC timeline effectively.
author: Bob Wayne

subject: series
synopsis: Fumita Yanagida's four-panel romantic comedy about tomboy Tomo Aizawa, hopelessly in love with her childhood friend Jun who sees her as 'one of the guys.' The strip's premise sounds thin but executes with genuine sweetness and increasingly sharp character development over its run.
author: Fumita Yanagida

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's definitive hardcover collection of Phase One Transformers comics, gathering the early IDW Transformers universe stories from writers including Simon Furman.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's 2015 mini based on the Robots in Disguise cartoon: Bumblebee's Autobots hunt escaped Decepticon prisoners on Earth.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW collected editions reprinting classic Marvel Comics Transformers stories, preserving the foundational Generation 1 comics in new trade paperback format.

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Hall and John Watkiss's Vertigo thriller about a tabloid reporter investigating a story that becomes much more dangerous than he expected in a conspiracy involving British intelligence.
author: Jason Hall

subject: series
synopsis: Al Ewing's patriotic Avengers team, a government-sponsored squad featuring American-themed heroes like Squirrel Girl, Cannonball, and Red Hulk, mixing political satire with classic superhero fun.
author: Al Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: Collected editions of the Ultimate Fantastic Four series, which reimagined Marvel's first family as teenage science prodigies in a contemporary Ultimate Universe setting with ambitious sci-fi concepts and a distinctly younger protagonist dynamic.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Charles Soule's run on Uncanny Inhumans, following Black Bolt and the expanding Inhuman nation during the height of Marvel's Inhumanity initiative, featuring cosmic-scale politics and the tensions of the Inhuman diaspora.
author: Charles Soule

subject: series
synopsis: Quality Comics' Golden Age anthology featuring Uncle Sam as a symbol of American heroism in wartime adventures, later absorbed into the DC universe. A product of the patriotic comics boom of the early 1940s.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's two mini-series (2006, 2007–2008) by Jimmy Palmiotti and Justin Gray reimagining the Freedom Fighters — Uncle Sam, Ray, Black Condor, Human Bomb, and others — as a covert government-sanction team navigating moral compromises and political intrigue. Sharp writing and impressive art elevated what might have been a simple nostalgia project.
author: Jimmy Palmiotti, Justin Gray

subject: series
synopsis: A prestige anthology series pairing the classic horror heroine with notable comics writers and artists, each bringing their own stylistic take to Vampirella's pulp horror mythology.

subject: series
synopsis: A modern continuation of the classic Vengeance of Vampirella horror series, reviving the tone of the original 1990s Harris Comics run with Vampirella at war against demonic forces threatening humanity.

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first vertical Infinity Comic tying into the Original Sin event, exploring Venom's dark history and the secrets unearthed by the Watcher's murder, in a format optimized for digital reading.

subject: series
synopsis: A tie-in miniseries to the Venom War crossover focusing on a supporting character drawn into the symbiote conflict, exploring personal stakes within the larger alien war narrative.

subject: series
synopsis: New 52 series featuring the Wildstorm-derived Voodoo character as a spy thriller about a Daemonite shapeshifter, struggling to find a consistent identity across two creative teams before cancellation.
author: Ron Marz

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis delivers a characteristically brutal and unsentimental World War I aviation story through the lens of a young American ace, examining the reality behind the myth of aerial heroism.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Tatsuhiko Takimoto and Kendi Oiwa's darkly comedic manga about Tatsuhiro Sato, a 22-year-old hikikomori (social recluse) who believes a secret organization is conspiring to keep him isolated. An uncomfortable, honest portrait of social anxiety and the struggle to re-engage with life.
author: Tatsuhiko Takimoto

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 26-volume hardcover collection of Will Eisner's original Spirit newspaper sections — one of the foundational texts of the comics medium. Eisner's mastery of page design, character, and literary ambition still astonishes, and these archives make the complete run accessible.
author: Will Eisner

subject: series
synopsis: Chuck Dixon's revival of Jorge Zaffino's 1987 post-apocalyptic frozen-world series follows a wandering scavenger protecting a young girl through a permanent ice age, delivering grim survival action with Chuck Dixon's efficient plotting.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Steampunk action series following Sterling Cross, a legendary monster hunter operating in a Victorian-era world threatened by supernatural creatures and secret societies.

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries by Paul Jenkins imagining the final days of Wolverine's long life, as an aged Logan confronts his greatest enemy in a melancholy meditation on his violent past and uncertain future.
author: Paul Jenkins

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron's acclaimed ongoing series following the Jean Grey School for Higher Learning under Wolverine's headmastership, delivering a funny, emotional, and action-packed celebration of X-Men history.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series
synopsis: A 1999 crossover miniseries pairing Marvel's two most lethal antiheroes as they investigate a shared enemy, combining Wolverine's berserker fury with the Punisher's methodical lethality.

subject: series
synopsis: An all-ages adventure in which a kid who is literally wrapped in bandages discovers he may be a mummy — or something stranger — while navigating middle school and uncovering the secret of his origins.
author: Joey Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries leading into the War of Kings event following the captive Vulcan and the Starjammers as they battle the Shi'ar Empire, setting the stage for the cosmic conflict to come.
author: Christopher Yost

subject: series
synopsis: A post-Apocalypse miniseries following the hunt for Scott Summers after his possession by Apocalypse, dealing with identity and the nature of the relationship between host and villain.
author: Joseph Harris

subject: series
synopsis: A four-issue crossover miniseries uniting the X-Men with the cosmic warriors of the Microverse, as both teams face a mysterious entity called the Entity with ties to the darkest parts of Charles Xavier's psyche.
author: Bill Mantlo

subject: series
synopsis: A five-issue limited series by Akira Yoshida and Paul Smith following Kitty Pryde and Lockheed to Japan, where Kitty faces ninja assassins and the legacy of her earliest adventures. Evocative of the classic Kitty Pryde and Wolverine limited series.
author: Akira Yoshida

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries following Pixie and her X-Men classmates on a trippy misadventure involving demonic forces and Pixie's mysterious heritage, blending teen drama with supernatural chaos.
author: Kathryn Immonen

subject: series
synopsis: Rob Liefeld's auxiliary Youngblood series presenting character profiles and backstory expansions for the early Image flagship team. A product of the Image era's merchandising mentality over storytelling substance.
author: Rob Liefeld

subject: series
synopsis: Joann Sfar and Lewis Trondheim's Dungeon Monstres: side stories of the monsters of their comic-fantasy Dungeon saga, drawn by guest artists.

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Niles' IDW anthology companion to 30 Days of Night, expanding the universe with vampire stories set beyond Barrow, Alaska. Varies in quality by creative team but maintains the franchise's stark, isolated horror atmosphere.
author: Steve Niles

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Lord of the Savage Land in various solo series — a Tarzan-analog with a saber-tooth companion Zabu navigating Ka-Zar's prehistoric Antarctic kingdom. The best material, by Bruce Jones, delivers smart pulp adventure.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Zombie World game/comic supplement.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2022-23 prestige one-shots, each a villain study — Riddler by Tom King and Mitch Gerads, Two-Face, Penguin, Mr. Freeze, Bane, Catwoman, Ra's al Ghul and Clayface.

subject: series
synopsis: Geof Darrow's elaborately detailed action comic.
author: Geof Darrow

subject: series
synopsis: Jack Kirby's 1977 Black Panther: T'Challa's wild cosmic-pulp adventures with King Solomon's Frog and the Collectors, later Ed Hannigan's issues.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite Entertainment's modern revival of the golden-age public-domain hero Black Terror, reinventing him for contemporary superhero storytelling across multiple series. Part of Dynamite's broader Project Superpowers universe reviving classic golden-age characters.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jack Kirby's DC series about four adventurers living on borrowed time. The Kirby originals are charming proto-Fantastic Four work; Howard Chaykin's 80s revival is more sophisticated.
author: Jack Kirby

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2001 four-issue Cyclops mini-series, part of the X-Men 'Icons' line of solo stories.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's adaptation of the classic pulp hero. Dennis O'Neil's version preserves the pulp adventure essence; the Dynamite revival by Roberson is equally faithful.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jo Duffy's 1987 series featuring the New Mutants and X-Factor Investigations in a lighter, comedic adventure involving a New York street gang of mutants, notable for early appearances of Ariel and the X-Terminators precursors.
author: Jo Duffy

subject: series
synopsis: Karl Kesel's 1996 Fantastic Four 2099: mysterious duplicates of the original Fantastic Four appear in the 2099 future, cut short when the line ended.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW ongoing G.I. Joe series focusing on covert black-ops missions by small specialized Joe teams, written by Chuck Dixon with a grittier military espionage tone.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning's 2001 four-issue Iceman mini, part of Marvel's Icons line.
author: Dan Abnett, Andy Lanning

subject: series
synopsis: David Mack's series follows a scarred government assassin in a near-future Japan as she questions her role; celebrated for its painterly mixed-media artwork and deeply literary exploration of identity, performance, and self-creation.
author: David Mack

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Millar and John Romita Jr.'s ultraviolent deconstruction of the superhero genre following a teenage boy who decides to become a real-life superhero with no powers, inadvertently inspiring others — including the lethal child vigilante Hit-Girl.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: A.J. Lieberman and Al Barrionuevo's 2006 Martian Manhunter mini: a darker J'onn J'onzz uncovers surviving Martians hidden on Earth.

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Wagner's solo series. The original Claremont 4-issue mini is a charming swashbuckling adventure; the various ongoings are more variable.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Anna Marie's various solo series. The character works best as supporting player — extended solos struggle with the untouchability premise. Howard Mackie's original limited series is charming.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's breakout original character - rogue archaeologist Aphra - stars in her own ongoing series navigating the criminal underworld, her complicated relationships, and ancient Force artifacts while staying one step ahead of the Empire and her own conscience.
author: Simon Spurrier

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis and Terry Dodson's 1996 four-issue Storm mini-series, stranding Ororo in another dimension.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's Brett Matthews adaptation is a serious-minded western revisiting of the character with genuine moral weight — who is the Lone Ranger, and what does his code cost him?
author: Brett Matthews

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Jensen and Arthur Ranson's 2002 X-Factor mini: human agents of a mutant civil-rights task force uncover a conspiracy within their own ranks.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and David Marquez's 2014 Miles Morales: Ultimate Spider-Man, Miles back in costume as the Ultimate Universe heads toward Secret Wars.

subject: series
synopsis: Hermes Press's chronological reprint of Lee Falk's The Phantom daily strip from 1936: the Ghost Who Walks in the jungles of Bengalla.
author: Lee  Falk

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Verheiden and Denis Beauvais's 1989 Aliens Book II: Newt and Hicks, now adults, confront a religious cult and an Earth overrun by Xenomorphs.
author: Mark Verheiden

subject: series
